Subject: Residency evidence request + VPC connectivity details (SOC2/SIG/CAIQ)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. As part of our procurement and security intake, our InfoSec team needs a compact evidence packet that confirms the following for MedServe's production scope:

- Confirmation that Redwood can pin customer data to EU regions (single-country preference where possible) and the procedural fallback if a node is unavailable (i.e., automatic fallback to another EU-only zone vs. cross-border).
- APAC hosting options and whether Azure/Oracle/other regional providers are supported for Private deployment.
- VPC / PrivateLink architecture for Private deployments: does traffic terminate in customer VPCs, what peering options exist, and operational runbooks for failover.
- SOC 2 attestations relevant to production inference, and any completed SIG/CAIQ answers you can share (redacted where necessary).

Could you provide a short reply with the above clarifications and attach a single ZIP with SOC2 summary, the SIG spreadsheet, and a diagram showing the PrivateLink/VPC topology? If some items require a follow-up security questionnaire, please point us to the right contact or form.

Deadline: we'd like the packet by EOD Tuesday (2027-04-06) to keep our procurement timeline.

Appreciate it — Olivia

--
Olivia Park
Head of Vendor Risk | MedServe Health
olivia.park@medserve.com

From: irene_choi@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Residency evidence request + VPC connectivity details (SOC2/SIG/CAIQ)

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Looping in Ben (solutions engineering) and Monica (security) to pull the artifacts and confirm the topology details. Short answers inline below; full packet coming as attachments once Monica confirms redaction rules.

- EU residency: Redwood supports pinning to EU regions and can restrict data plane and inference nodes to EU zones. For critical production workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments — Hosted API falls back to pooled nodes but we can provide region affinity and SLA-backed routing controls. Fallback policy: if the primary EU zone is unavailable, we route to a designated standby EU zone; cross-border fallback (EU -> US/APAC) only occurs under explicit customer-approved escalation and we document the exact trigger thresholds.

- APAC: Private deployments are supported on selected cloud partners in APAC. We have pre-validated images for AWS ap-southeast-1 and GCP/AK regions in Japan/Sydney for Private, and can engage our infra partners for Azure/Oracle if required.

- VPC/PrivateLink: customer-managed VPC peering or PrivateLink (cloud-specific) are both supported. For Private deployments the inference nodes can be deployed inside customer VPC with optional transit gateways. We have an ops runbook for peering, failover, and keystore handoff (HSM/KMS guidance) — Monica will attach the runbook and the diagram.

- SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ: we can share the SOC 2 summary report and completed SIG XLSX; CAIQ responses are included where applicable. Where redaction is required (e.g., exact IP inventories), Monica will coordinate a redacted pack or a controlled Dataroom link.

We aim to get the packet to you by Monday EOD PT; if that misses your internal deadline, we can prioritize the SOC2 + topology diagram first.

Thanks — Irene

--
Irene Choi
Director, Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Residency evidence request + VPC connectivity details (SOC2/SIG/CAIQ)

Hi Olivia — quick tech notes to supplement Irene's summary:

- Deployment modes: Dedicated (reserved pools) and Private (VPC-hosted) are the paths to full residency guarantees. For Dedicated we can reserve capacity scoped to an EU-only fleet; Dedicated will not cross-border unless explicitly configured.

- Peering specifics: On AWS we use AWS PrivateLink for control-plane connections and optional ENIs in customer VPCs for data-plane isolation; on GCP we recommend VLAN attachments + VPC peering. For cross-cloud Private deployments we provision VPN tunnels with route filtering.

- Failover semantics: the runtime prefers in-region KV cache warmers to minimize cold-start impact; failover to a standby EU zone preserves cached prefixes where possible but the runtime will rebuild KV caches on first requests — we document expected latency degradation in the runbook.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want a topology walkthrough.

- Ben

Attachments referenced: privatelink_diagram.png (diagram stub)
